work.title: Scheherazade
work.movement: III. The Young Prince and the Young Princess

version.note: The recording source does not identify a performing edition or arrangement.

date.note: These dates describe the complete suite’s sessions; no source assigns this movement to one of the two days.

place.value: War Memorial Opera House, San Francisco

catalogue.note: Album number of the original Victor 78 rpm set, not an individual side or matrix number.

matrixTakeSides.note: The sources identify album DM-920 but give no matrices, take numbers or side allocation for this movement. The supplied cover image does not resolve them.

credits.value: Bob Varney — transfer from the original Victor 78 rpm set
credits.note: Commons additionally describes the file as restored, without naming a separate restoration engineer.

date.note: The Archive item was made public on 19 August 2009, but the transfer date itself is not stated.

processing.value: Transferred from the original Victor 78 rpm set; described on Commons as restored
processing.note: Stylus, equalisation, speed correction, noise reduction and side-join settings are not documented.

digital.format: MP3 access derivative of the Wikimedia Commons Ogg Vorbis file

composition.value: Public domain in jurisdictions applying an unextended life-plus-70-year term
composition.note: Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov died in 1908. This assessment concerns the original composition, not a later edition, arrangement or this recording; it is not a worldwide rights clearance.

recording.value: CC0 1.0 designation on Commons; public-domain dedication at the upstream Archive item
recording.note: These are the digital-file sources’ rights statements. They do not by themselves demonstrate that the uploader could waive all rights in the underlying 1942 Victor recording; no independent United States clearance is established here.

rights.creditLine: Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov: Scheherazade, Op. 35, III. The Young Prince and the Young Princess — San Francisco Symphony Orchestra, Pierre Monteux; Naoum Blinder, violin. Victor DM-920, recorded 3–4 March 1942. Transfer by Bob Varney, Internet Archive, via Wikimedia Commons; the file is designated CC0, with underlying recording rights not independently cleared.
